issue_context.title: tcp: write: broken pipe: [E] Render failed: failed to render template + [E] plainTextInternal (status=500)
issue_context.body:
### Description

In the log it show the following:

2024/04/30 23:21:27 .../context_response.go:87:HTML() [E] Render failed: failed to render template: home, error: write tcp 127.0.0.1:3000->127.0.0.1:50284: write: broken pipe
2024/04/30 23:21:27 .../context_response.go:89:HTML() [E] plainTextInternal (status=500): write bytes failed: write tcp 127.0.0.1:3000->127.0.0.1:50284: write: broken pipe

Installed via docker compose on Synology NAS.

### Gitea Version

gitea-1.22.0

### Can you reproduce the bug on the Gitea demo site?

No

### Log Gist

_No response_

### Screenshots

![log](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/assets/40196995/c4df7d11-60ff-4f70-a9ed-c82f383ced60)


### Git Version

_No response_

### Operating System

Synology DSM

### How are you running Gitea?

Docker Container

### Database

None

### Additional remarks
I already did this setting: Administration -> Konfiguration -> Einstellungen -> Gravatar deaktivieren
comments: If you didn't experience any problem during usage, it's safe to ignore them . It is a false alarm. Some error messages are reported too aggressively.

If there are some problems when browsing the pages ..... it looks more like an OS/envorinment related problem.

Usually `write: broken pipe` means the TCP connection breaks too early (in most cases, it shouldn't be related to Gitea itself)

ok, thanks for the info. I didn't have any problems in usage and only saw this message in the logs.
Feel free to close this issue when you want to close this issue

->  Ignore uesless error message "broken pipe" #30801 

Let's make Gitea never show such useless logs 😁

review_comments: Is there no other way to detect this apart from ignoring errors completely?
The question is: why do you want to do so? What would you like to do when the "Write" fails .......... I do not see any useful case to handle such error.
I think we can merge it as-is, if there would be any real requirement to see the "errors", we can improve it then
Will this work on Windows? My impression is that the syscall package is unix only.

It is a common package.

Windows also have similar concept "syscall"

![image](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/assets/2114189/2449f561-3982-4314-8faf-814a4119ae5a)
Yeah looks like there is some form of [stub module](https://go.dev/src/syscall/syscall_windows.go) for windows syscall. I don't think it could emit EPIPE there but at least it will compile.
